criteria.name: Runs PostgreSQL in production (schema design, indexes, query plans)
criteria.justification: The role owns the persistence layer; nobody on the team does today.

anchors.0: No relational database work in production, or only via a warehouse/analytics tool.
anchors.1: Used a relational DB in production through an ORM without owning schema or performance; or production MySQL/SQL Server only.
anchors.2: Designed schemas and indexes for a production PostgreSQL database.
anchors.3: Owned production PostgreSQL: schema, indexing strategy, plans, capacity.

criteria.name: Ships schema and data migrations on live data safely
criteria.justification: Migrations run at app start today and a PK type rewrite was done in place.

anchors.1: Generated or applied routine migrations (e.g. autogenerate) on small or non-production data.
anchors.2: Wrote and shipped migrations on production data, including data backfills.
anchors.3: Designed online/zero-downtime migrations (expand-contract, batched backfills, concurrent index builds) on large tables.

anchors.1: Mentions optimisation or indexing without specifics.
anchors.2: Concrete fixes: EXPLAIN-driven indexing, removing N+1, keyset pagination, with outcomes.
anchors.3: Systematic performance work with measured results at scale (slow-query monitoring, partitioning, plan regressions).

criteria.name: Production Python with an ORM (SQLAlchemy/SQLModel ideal)

anchors.0: No evidence of Python or of any ORM.
anchors.1: Production ORM work in another language, or Python scripting without an ORM.
anchors.2: Production Python with SQLAlchemy, SQLModel or the Django ORM.
anchors.3: Deep SQLAlchemy/SQLModel work: session management, relationship loading strategies, typed models.

anchors.0: No evidence of testing database code.
anchors.1: Wrote tests that touch a database.
anchors.2: Built isolated DB tests: per-test transactions/rollback, fixtures, containers.
anchors.3: Designed the test strategy for DB code across a team (Testcontainers, migration tests, CI databases).

criteria.name: Zero-downtime deploys with schema changes and multiple replicas

anchors.1: Took part in deployments that included schema changes.
anchors.2: Separated migrations from app rollout, or ran backward-compatible deploys across replicas.
anchors.3: Owned the deploy process for schema changes at scale (expand-contract across services, rollback plans).

criteria.name: PostgreSQL operations: backups, pooling, replication, monitoring

anchors.1: Used a managed database service and its built-in backups/metrics.
anchors.2: Configured one or more of: PgBouncer, replication, backup/restore, slow-query monitoring.
anchors.3: Ran Postgres HA and recovery (Patroni, pgBackRest, tested restores, failover).

anchors.1: Async web frameworks without async DB access.
anchors.2: Production asyncpg or async SQLAlchemy, or equivalent async drivers in another language.
anchors.3: Migrated a service from sync to async DB access with measured gains.

exclusions: name, photo, age, date of birth, gender, nationality, marital status, religion, disability
university or employer prestige as a standalone signal
years of experience as a requirement
data warehouse / analytics tooling counted toward must-haves (anti-goal)
